hook: Masayoshi Son founded SoftBank in 1981 as a personal computer software distributor and has built it into a global investment group whose stated goal is to lead in artificial superintelligence. SoftBank bought the chip designer Arm in 2016, and Son chairs it. In 2025 he became chairman of the Stargate Project, which plans to invest $500 billion in AI infrastructure for OpenAI in the United States, and SoftBank agreed to invest up to $40 billion in OpenAI itself.

quick_facts: Born in Tosu, Saga Prefecture, Japan, in 1957, he moved to California as a teenager and graduated in economics from the University of California, Berkeley, in 1980.
He founded Nihon SoftBank, now SoftBank Group Corp., in September 1981 and is its Representative Director, Corporate Officer, Chairman and CEO.
In April 2006 he became chairman and chief executive of Vodafone K.K., now SoftBank Corp., the group's Japanese telecommunications company, where he remains a board director.
He has chaired Arm since SoftBank acquired it in 2016 and stayed on as chairman of Arm Holdings plc through its Nasdaq listing in September 2023.
Since 2017 he has invested through the SoftBank Vision Funds.
TIME named him to its 2024 list of the 100 most influential people in AI.

achievements.title: Founder, SoftBank Group
achievements.impact: Grew a software distribution business founded in 1981 into a holding company spanning telecommunications, chip design and technology investment.

achievements.title: Chairman, Arm
achievements.impact: Led Arm's board after SoftBank bought the chip designer in 2016. When Nvidia's agreed purchase of Arm was called off in February 2022 over regulatory obstacles, SoftBank listed Arm on Nasdaq in September 2023.

achievements.title: Chairman, The Stargate Project
achievements.impact: Chairs the venture announced in January 2025 with OpenAI, Oracle and MGX as equity funders, with SoftBank holding financial responsibility and OpenAI operational responsibility.

achievements.title: OpenAI investment
achievements.impact: SoftBank agreed on March 31, 2025, to follow-on investments of up to $40 billion in OpenAI, planning to syndicate $10 billion to co-investors, on top of $2.2 billion invested through Vision Fund 2 since September 2024.
